Yes — a portable power station can work as a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) for your computer, but only if it supports fast, automatic switchover to battery power. A regular portable power station is not necessarily suitable.

According to Anker SOLIX’s UPS guidance, you should verify the model’s transfer time, automatic switchover, pass-through operation, output capacity, and battery capacity.

What matters most

Feature

	

What to look for




Automatic switchover

	

Switches to battery without you doing anything




Transfer time

	

Ideally a documented time of 10 ms or less, if your computer can tolerate it




Output waveform

	

Pure sine wave AC output




Pass-through operation

	

Can power your computer while plugged into wall power and keep the battery ready




Capacity

	

Enough watt-hours (Wh) for your desired backup runtime

A transfer time of 10–20 ms may work with many computers, but compatibility isn't guaranteed. For critical systems that require zero interruption, a dedicated online UPS is safer. See Anker SOLIX’s explanation of transfer-time limits.

Portable power stations worth considering

1. EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus

A promising compact option because EcoFlow specifically identifies this model as supporting NAS-standard UPS functionality.

Important: Confirm the exact transfer time and compatibility with your computer before buying.

Listed capacity: 2,073.6 Wh · Switchover: ≤15 ms

My recommendation

If your main goal is to prevent your desktop computer from shutting down during a brief outage, I would prioritize a dedicated UPS unless a portable power station explicitly supports UPS mode with a transfer time your computer can tolerate. If you also want hours of backup power during extended outages, a UPS-capable power station may be a better fit.

One question that would help me narrow it down: Are you backing up a desktop PC or a laptop?
